-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol  Corea, Administrative Assistant at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”

Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The Meeting Host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city/agendas.

MINUTES
  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  NOVEMBER 17, 2020

1.  CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Schmitz, Addleman, Arata, Buresh, Carman,
  Carrese,  Corman,  Shinn,  Stegura,
  Zuckerman

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Bayer, Medawar, Seamans, Silvano

  STUDENT MEMBERS PRESENT:  Scandaliato

  STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Greg Grammer, City Manager
  David Wahba, Director of Community Development
  and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  ALSO PRESENT:  Surabhi Barbhaya, Senior Planner, Michael Baker International
  John Bellas, Principal, Michael Baker International
  Robert Davis, Michael Baker International
  Dan Wery, Principal Community Planner, Michael Baker
  International

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES,
  OCTOBER 20, 2020.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CORMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER ARATA
to,
  APPROVE THE GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  OCTOBER 20, 2020.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  CITYWIDE LAND USE DISCUSSION - SURVEY RESULTS, PARKING STUDY
  HIGHLIGHTS, LAND USE ALTERNATIVES DISCUSSION.
John Bellas, Micheal Baker International (MBI), provided an overview of the items that will be
discussed.

Surabhi Barbhaya (MBI) introduced the fourth meeting of the Land Use Elements, which will
include a discussion on Citywide Land Use Alternatives and Policies.

Robert Davis (MBI) began with a presentation on the Parking Study findings, which included the
following:

  •  There are 5,868 off-street parking spaces

  o  Area 1 (includes the Peninsula Shopping Center and The Promenade on the
  Peninsula) The parking provided is 3,373 parking spaces.
  o  Area 2 – (includes a mix of smaller parking lots). The parking provided is 2,495
  parking spaces.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  1
 MINUTES, NOVEMBER 17, 2020
   •  There are 497 on-street parking spaces

  •  The supply meets the code requirements.

  o  The code requirement for Area 1 = 3,284 (surplus of 89 parking spaces)
  o  The code requirement for Area 2 = 2,641 (deficiency of -57 parking spaces)

  •  Parking rate > ULI (Urban Land Institute) and ITE (Institute of Transportation Engineering)

Mr. Davis stated that the parking rate in the City is higher than the rate in the ULI or ITE in a
number of categories; primarily in the area of general commercial, banks, restaurants/bars. The
excess in the parking rate can vary between 20-30% and although the findings showed a slight
deficiency when compared to the code requirement, there is actually a parking surplus when
looking at parking demands that are likely to occur with the existing land uses.

Mr. Davis provided recommendations, including:

  •  Modernize commercial district parking rates.
  •  Encourage mixed use projects with shared parking.
  •  Develop shared public parking facilities with “park once” strategy, so that people can park
  in one location and then walk to the different parts of the district.
  •  Allow new development to pay “in-lieu” parking fees for a portion of the on-site parking
  requirement to fund shared public parking facilities.
  •  Consider the formation of a parking benefit district as an alternative to the in-lieu parking
  fee approach.

Phase two will include analyzing future parking requirements for the commercial district according
to the recommended land use mix and develop a recommended parking demand management
strategy.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked for the ULI and ITE rates. Mr. Davis stated that the
recommended rates for general commercial would be 4 per 1,000 and the city is at 5 per 1,000;
for restaurants, the existing rate is 28.57 per 1,000 sq. ft. of seating area and the recommended
is 20 per 1,000 sq. ft. of seating area.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that at the Peninsula Shopping Center, in the major
parking fields, there is insufficient parking. Mr. Davis stated that their analysis looks at the likely
parking demand for the uses in the shopping center and could not perform a parking utilization
survey; therefore, the best methodology was to look at the ULI and ITE recommendations for what
parking demand is likely to be, and when comparing the code requirement with the supply that is
there, it is parked above code.

CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that available parking depends on how close one chooses to be to the
place being visited.

Director Wahba stated that the parking requirements have been and continue to be very
conservative and one of the implementation measures to look at in the General Plan is to consider
better use of shared parking and looking at reducing parking requirement, in some categories, by
20%.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER CARRESE, Director Wahba stated that he
will go back and take a look to see if the Anastasi project at 927 Deep Valley Drive was taken into
consideration.

Ms. Barbhaya provided the results of the Commercial District Concepts and Ideas Survey.

  •  Opportunities for improving overall conncectivity within and around the Commercial
  District.

  o  Nodes at 5-minute walking distance and Smaller block pattern received the
  most support.
  o  Connection to southwest or northeast neighborhoods received the least
  support.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  2
 MINUTES, NOVEMBER 17, 2020
 COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that the topographical separation between the
neighborhoods and the commercial district could be difficult. The only location that could work
would be the neighborhoods within walking distance to the shopping center.

CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that if there was a connection from the neighborhoods to the commercial
district, such as a meandering path that did not have steep elevation or stairs, then the
connectivity could occur and could be used as a place to exercise.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that this would be a specialized use and the survey
seemed to be looking for general connectivity from the neighborhoods to the shopping center.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARMAN expressed that she was surprised that the high school
population was not included in the study since half of students do not drive and are limited to that
area to walk to, after school.

CHAIR SCHMITZ commented that given different entry points, the survey questions regarding
neighborhood connectivity, may have been answered differently.
  • Opportunities for improvements and infill in Peninsula Center site.

  o  The two choices given were, pockets of greenspace/plazas, which received the
  most support, followed by infill development to frame streets, which did not receive
  much support.

Mr. Bellas asked committee members, if the scale of the buildings in the drawings were smaller,
would that have changed their answer to the survey question.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER FRIEDMAN, Mr. Bellas stated that what
planners and landscape planners have observed, is that if you define the public realm with
buildings or with other defined barriers, people are more likely to participate in that space as
pedestrians.

Ms. Barbhaya added that when pedestrian interest is created, then it encourages walking, since
it will seem shorter.

Mr. Wery stated that the main difference when referring to framing the street is putting the
buildings closer to the sidewalk as opposed to placing the parking closer to the sidewalk.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN expressed his concern with the drawing which shows a
large scale building and green space taking the place of needed parking.

Mr. Bellas stated that the intention is that any new buildings built will still be required to have
adequate and sufficient parking. If there is new construction, should policies be in place to steer
the design of the building in a way to frame pieces of the center.

  •  Opportunities for repuposing the Promenade Mall building.

  o  Most support was received to repurpose the building for a large central plaze
  space, followed by dividing the Promenade Mall’s mass. The least support was
  received to repurpose the building to reconnect Deep Valley Drive and for the
  redevelopment of underutilized property.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that this will require removing a lot of buildings in
the promenade and asked why someone would give up this much floor area, unless it were
required. Would this imply that the city would be trading right-of-way on Deep Valley Drive?

Director Wahba stated that a new development agreement would be envisioned where the city
would have the ability to work with the developer to get the street back.

  •  Opportunities for improving street frontage of current Promenade Mall building.

  o  Most support was received to enhance the Promenade Mall and to create a
  midblock crossing, followed by, activate with a liner building along the garage.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARMAN commented on the scale and the existing three-story buildings
that are adjacent to the mall; if you look to the east you don’t see much due to the height of the
 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  3
 MINUTES, NOVEMBER 17, 2020
 buildings. COMMMITTEE MEMBER CARMAN expressed her concern with how this would tie in
with the character of the community.

Ms. Barbhaya stated that how a building is designed creates the illusion of scale.

Mr. Bellas stated that looking at the Promenade Mall from Silver Spur Road, there is no distinction
between the floors. Differentiation from the ground floors to the floors above it minimizes the
perception of mass of a building.

In response to a comment by COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Ms. Barbhaya stated that
a second conceptual design will be introduced that does not include the Promenade Mall.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARRESE suggested keeping the commercial area two-story and
making the gathering area on the roof top.

  •  Opportunities for development of Brick Walk property on top of the bluff

  o  Most responses were in support of creating lookout opportunities and creating
  a pedestrian connection, followed by creating a complimentary liner building
  and the redevelopment of the underutilized property.

  •  Opportunities for development on North side of Silver Spur Road

  o  There was 50/50 support for consolidating Silver Spur Road and Bart Earl Way.

Ms. Barbhaya stated that there is 120 ft. between Silver Spur Road and Bart Earl Way and there
are six lanes. Typically for the amount of traffic in that area, there would be a need for two lanes
and a turning lane. The idea would be to eliminate Bart Earl Way, put buildings in front, and create
a double-sided commercial street.

  o  Most responses were in support of using Bart Earl Way ROW as an incentives.

Ms. Barbhaya stated that using right-of-way as an incentive, would mean that Silver Spur Road
and Bart Earl Way would be consolidated.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN expressed his concern with the issues with the grade
separation in the area in order to accomplish this. Director Wahba provided some explanation on
how this could be done. Vacating Bart Earl Way would be an incentive to property owners,
because of the additional land acquisition. This is a conceptual plan that may work in the future,
but there are definitely challenges.

A brief discussion ensued.

Mr. Wery added that there will be an implementation plan, which will follow the General Plan.

Mr. Wery provided a presentation on Land Use Alternatives. In previous discussions, two school
properties were identified as opportunity sites for staff or low income housing. One more
opportunity site is being introduced for consideration at Rolling Hills Covenant Church, which
could be developed the same way as the school sites.
CHAIR SCHMITZ commented that the school sites are not under the City’s jurisdiction and the
church is a private property. Mr. Wery stated that if the school or church wanted to do this, then
the policy would be in place to encourage this.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Ms. Barbhaya stated that
Kelley’s Corner is in the landmark overlay, however, the property behind it could be developed.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS expressed concern with ingress/egress from the schools or church in
case of an emergency. CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that the church site has the benefit of being able
to go out onto Western.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARRESE commented that the smaller church parcel could be used as
low income housing. COMMITTEE MEMBER FRIEDMAN concurred.

In a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Mr. Wery stated that this could be used
as a potential site to meet RHNA numbers.
 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  4
 MINUTES, NOVEMBER 17, 2020
 Mr. Wery provided an overview of the areas proposed to be changed to a different land use
designation. A significant change is recommended at the north end of Highridge Road where it
would go from commercial office to neighborhood commercial. In addition the site behind City Hall
which could go to neighborhood commercial.

In a response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Mr. Wery stated that the
reason they are not going to neighborhood residential is that they are already adjacent to non-
residential uses.

Ms. Barbhaya stated that neighborhood commercial will still allow for residential.

Mr. Wery further provided the changes that are proposed the be made to the land use
designations, including the mixed-use overlaty zone.

6.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

NONE

7.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR SCHMITZ thanked the committee and adjourned the meeting at 8:06 p.m. The next
General Plan Advisory Committee meeting will be held on Tuesday, December 1, 2020 at via
Video Teleconference.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Velveth Schmitz, Chair
